title: Phishing Awareness
what_is_it: Deceptive messages (email, SMS, chat, QR codes) designed to make you reveal credentials, pay money or open something unsafe.
why_it_matters: Phishing is a leading way accounts get taken over; one click can expose a whole organisation.
warning_signs: Sender domain that only looks like the real one
Request for a password or code
Link whose real destination differs from the text
Impersonation of a boss, bank or IT desk
Unexpected QR code asking you to sign in
safe_practices: Hover over links to preview them (do not click)
Verify through an official channel you already trust
Report the message using your organisation's reporting method
if_something_happens: If you clicked: disconnect nothing yourself, report it immediately
Change the password from a trusted device and enable MFA
Tell IT/security what you entered and when

safe_examples.label: Suspicious (fictional)
safe_examples.text: From: it-support@mail-helpdesk.invalid - 'Your mailbox will close in 1 hour. Confirm your password at the link below.' Signs: look-alike sender, urgency, credential request.

safe_examples.label: Suspicious (fictional)
safe_examples.text: 'Invoice attached - please pay today to avoid penalty.' From an unknown sender with an unexpected attachment. Signs: payment pressure, unexpected attachment.

safe_examples.label: Safer behaviour
safe_examples.text: You get a message you did not expect. You do not click. You open the official website yourself or call the number on your card, and you report the message.

title: Password Security
what_is_it: A password is a secret that proves who you are to a service.
why_it_matters: Reused or weak passwords let one breach unlock many accounts.
warning_signs: Passwords shared in chat or notes
Notification of a breach involving your email
safe_practices: Use a long unique passphrase per account
Check if your accounts appear in breach-notification services
if_something_happens: Change the password on the affected site and any site where it was reused
Enable MFA
Review recent sign-in activity

title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
what_is_it: MFA asks for a second proof (app code, security key, passkey) in addition to your password.
why_it_matters: A strong password plus MFA is generally safer than a password alone because a stolen password is not enough.
warning_signs: Unexpected MFA prompts you did not trigger
Requests to read out a one-time code
Pressure to approve a prompt quickly
safe_practices: Prefer authenticator apps or security keys over SMS where possible
Learn about passkeys/WebAuthn: phishing-resistant sign-in bound to the real website
Deny prompts you did not start
if_something_happens: If you approved a prompt by mistake, change your password and report it
Review registered MFA devices and remove unknown ones

title: Social Engineering
what_is_it: Manipulating people (phone, chat, in person) into bypassing normal security steps.
why_it_matters: Attackers target trust and helpfulness because people are often easier to influence than systems.
warning_signs: Pretext stories with pressure to skip process
Caller claims to be IT or an executive
Offers that seem too good to be true
safe_practices: Verify identity using a known official number or channel
Follow the standard process even when pressured
It is fine to say 'I will call you back'
if_something_happens: Stop the conversation
Report what was asked and by whom
Change credentials if any were shared

title: Safe Browsing
what_is_it: Habits that reduce risk from websites, downloads and browser extensions.
why_it_matters: Malicious or spoofed sites can steal data or deliver unwanted software.
warning_signs: Login pages reached via an unexpected link
safe_practices: Type known addresses or use bookmarks for sensitive sites
Install only trusted extensions and software
if_something_happens: Close the tab, do not enter details
Run your approved security scan
Change passwords if you entered any

title: Secure Wi-Fi
what_is_it: Using wireless networks in a way that protects your traffic and devices.
why_it_matters: Open or fake hotspots can expose traffic or lure users to spoofed pages.
warning_signs: Hotspot with a name similar to a known one
Open network asking you to sign in with work credentials
safe_practices: Use a VPN approved by your organisation on public Wi-Fi
Turn off auto-join for open networks
Forget networks you no longer use
if_something_happens: Disconnect and switch networks
Change passwords used while connected
Report if work data may have been exposed

title: Software Updates
what_is_it: Installing security patches for operating systems, apps and devices.
why_it_matters: Many attacks rely on known weaknesses that updates already fix.
safe_practices: Remove software you no longer use
Install updates only from official sources
if_something_happens: Update now if you have postponed
Ask IT about unsupported software
Report fake update pop-ups

title: Ransomware Awareness
what_is_it: Malware that locks or encrypts data and demands payment, often alongside data-theft threats.
why_it_matters: It can halt operations for days and cause permanent data loss.
safe_practices: Keep offline or immutable backups and test restores
Be cautious with attachments and links
if_something_happens: Disconnect the device from the network as instructed by your policy and report immediately
Do not pay or negotiate on your own
Follow the incident-response plan

title: USB / Removable Media Safety
what_is_it: Safe handling of USB drives and other portable storage.
why_it_matters: Unknown drives can carry malware, and lost drives can leak data.
warning_signs: Drives that prompt to run programs
if_something_happens: Do not use the device; hand it to IT/security
Report lost drives straight away

title: Data Privacy
what_is_it: Collecting, sharing and storing personal data responsibly.
why_it_matters: Mishandled data harms people and can lead to legal and reputational damage.
warning_signs: Over-sharing in forms or social posts
Data sent to the wrong recipient
if_something_happens: Remove access and report accidental disclosure
Note what data and who was affected

title: Mobile Security
what_is_it: Protecting phones and tablets and the data and accounts on them.
why_it_matters: Phones hold email, banking and MFA apps, so they are high-value targets.
warning_signs: SMS links claiming package or bank issues
safe_practices: Use a screen lock and device encryption
Install apps from official stores only
if_something_happens: Lock/wipe a lost device remotely
Change key passwords
Report to IT if work data was on it

title: Remote Work Security
what_is_it: Working securely from home or while travelling.
why_it_matters: Home networks and shared spaces are less controlled than office networks.
warning_signs: Shared family devices used for work
safe_practices: Secure the home router and change defaults
Keep work and personal data separate
if_something_happens: Report lost or stolen equipment immediately
Change passwords if a device was shared or compromised

title: Cloud Account Security
what_is_it: Protecting accounts for email, storage and SaaS services.
why_it_matters: Cloud accounts are reachable from anywhere, so stolen sign-ins have wide impact.
safe_practices: Review sign-in activity and connected apps
if_something_happens: Sign out all sessions and reset the password
Remove unknown apps and rules
Report to your security team

title: Incident Reporting
what_is_it: Telling the right people quickly when something looks wrong.
why_it_matters: Early reports let security teams contain issues before they spread.
safe_practices: Describe what you saw, not what you assume
Keep evidence such as the original email
if_something_happens: Report immediately - you will not be blamed for good-faith reports
Follow instructions from the security team

title: AI-Enabled Scam Awareness
what_is_it: Scams that use AI to imitate voices, faces or writing styles.
why_it_matters: Convincing fakes make impersonation of managers or relatives more believable.
warning_signs: Unexpected urgent request in a familiar voice or video
safe_practices: Verify through a second, trusted channel
Treat urgent money requests with extra caution
Limit publicly shared voice and video
if_something_happens: Stop and verify before acting
Report the attempt
If money was sent, contact your bank at once
